label: Established psychoanalytic feminism and formulated the lateral sibling axis in psychic development
description: Juliet Mitchell formulated the lateral axis of sibling relationships as an autonomous matrix of desire and rivalry alongside parental verticality.
historicalContext: Initiated in 'Psychoanalysis and Feminism' (1974) and crystallized in 'Siblings: Sex and Violence' (2003).
dialecticalTension: Shifting psychoanalysis from an exclusively vertical parental genealogy to an intersubjective lateral field of peer trauma and solidarity.

label: Reclaimed Freud's drive theory and castration complex as an analysis of patriarchal culture
description: Mitchell fundamentally rescued Sigmund Freud from feminist dismissal by showing that psychoanalysis describes patriarchal mechanisms rather than endorsing them.
historicalContext: Published in 'Psychoanalysis and Feminism' (1974), transforming modern feminist theory across Europe and the Americas.
dialecticalTension: Distinguishing between Freud's descriptive diagnostic account of patriarchal culture and a prescriptive ideological doctrine.

label: Integrated Beauvoir's existential feminist critique with psychoanalytic depth structuralism
description: Mitchell synthesized Simone de Beauvoir's insight that 'one is not born, but rather becomes, a woman' with Freudian and Lacanian unconscious mechanisms.
historicalContext: Mitchell engaged Beauvoir's critique of psychoanalysis in 'The Second Sex', showing how structural psychoanalysis answers Beauvoir's existential inquiry.
dialecticalTension: Existential conscious choice versus the deep unconscious internalization of patriarchal symbolic structures.
